document_title: Two names hold 74 percent of the 3,164 automated vehicles on the TxDMV report
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Waymo lists 1,259. International Transport Eng lists 7.

Both sit on one report from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, data as of October 29th. It counts 3,164 automated vehicles from 17 companies. Waymo and Tesla Robotaxi hold 74 percent of them.

Since May 28th a company running automated vehicles commercially in Texas needs a state authorization. It carries no fee and never expires.

The City of Dallas asked the department to require crash history. The department answered that the Transportation Code doesn't allow it.

A concern that an automated vehicle could cause serious bodily injury or death can go to the department's Enforcement Division. Below that standard it calls administrative enforcement unlikely.

Each car in the lot on the slides stands for ten listed vehicles.

Should lawmakers let the department require crash history?

#TxDMV #SB2807 #CityOfDallas

S1.headline: 3,164 automated vehicles, 17 names
S1.body: Since May 28th, a company running automated vehicles commercially in Texas needs a state authorization. A Texas Department of Motor Vehicles report with data as of October 29th lists 17 companies.
strings: Since May 28th, a company running automated vehicles commercially in Texas needs a state authorization. A Texas Department of Motor Vehicles report with data as of October 29th lists 17 companies.

S2.headline: Two names hold 74 percent
S2.body: Waymo lists 1,259 vehicles and Tesla Robotaxi 1,080. The other 15 companies share 825. One car here stands for ten listed vehicles, rounded, and never fewer than one.
strings: Waymo lists 1,259 vehicles and Tesla Robotaxi 1,080. The other 15 companies share 825. One car here stands for ten listed vehicles, rounded, and never fewer than one.

S3.headline: Fifteen companies share 825
S3.cite: c2 c1 c7 c15 c6 c19
S3.body: Avride lists 344. Then 14 companies list fewer than 100 each, down to International Transport Eng at 7. One car stands for ten listed vehicles, and a white bar marks where each company ends.

S4.headline: The smallest entry lists 7
S4.body: International Transport Eng lists 7 vehicles. It draws as the lot's last car, alone in a row built for ten. Bot Auto and Waabi list 13 each, MOIA and PlusAI 12 each.
strings: International Transport Eng lists 7 vehicles. It draws as the lot's last car, alone in a row built for ten. Bot Auto and Waabi list 13 each, MOIA and PlusAI 12 each.

S5.headline: No fee, and no expiry
S5.body: Commercial operation has needed an authorization since May 28th, 154 days before the report's data date. It carries no fee and stays valid until the department revokes it.
strings: Commercial operation has needed an authorization since May 28th, 154 days before the report's data date. It carries no fee and stays valid until the department revokes it.

S6.headline: Dallas asked for crash history
S6.body: In comments on the rules, the City of Dallas asked the department to require crash history and to make information about approved operators public. The department answered that sections 545.453 and 545.456 of the Transportation Code don't allow it to require crash history.
strings: In comments on the rules, the City of Dallas asked the department to require crash history and to make information about approved operators public. The department answered that sections 545.453 and 545.456 of the Transportation Code don't allow it to require crash history.

S7.headline: The line is serious bodily injury
S7.body: The department treats an operation as endangering the public when it has caused serious bodily injury or is likely to. It calls administrative enforcement unlikely below that standard. Traffic laws apply to these vehicles as to any other.
strings: The line is serious bodily injury

S8.headline: On two freight lanes, a person sits up front
S8.body: Volvo says its autonomous hauls with Waabi between Dallas and Houston currently run with an observer in the driver's seat. Kodiak and Charger say they run between Dallas and Laredo with a safety driver behind the wheel.

S9.headline: Where a concern goes
S9.body: A concern that an automated vehicle could cause serious bodily injury or death can go to the department's Enforcement Division at txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop. The program page links an authorizations report dated October 29th.
